title: The same difference from a study four times the size: standard error 2.07
alt: Narrow bell curve centred on 9.0 mg/dL with the region from 4.9 to 13.1 shaded, drawn on the same axis as the earlier wider curve.
longDescription: This curve keeps the observed difference of 9.0 mg/dL and the within-group standard deviation of 16 mg/dL, and raises the group sizes from 30 people each to 120 people each. The standard error falls from 4.13 to 2.07 mg/dL, so the curve is about half as wide as the one earlier in this lesson. The shaded band runs from 4.9 to 13.1 mg/dL and again covers the middle 95% of the curve. Because the standard error halved, the band is half as wide as the one on the earlier chart, 8.2 mg/dL against 16.2. The horizontal axis is the same as the earlier chart, so the two shaded bands can be compared directly. The no-difference value of 0 mg/dL is marked and now sits far outside the band, more than four standard errors below the centre. Four times the people bought half the width, and nothing else about the study changed.
